rule: A benchmark is an order of magnitude displayed next to the deck figure, with its source and date. It never enters the score. An entry with an empty value means no dated source was found; it is kept so the gap is visible. Entries marked all_models are stage-generic (burn, runway, round) and are also shown for the other models.

metric.fr: Rule of 40

series_b.value: growth rate plus profit should add up to 40 %; year-over-year MRR or ARR growth, EBITDA as the profit baseline (or operating income, net income, free cash flow); written for SaaS companies at scale, at least 50M USD of revenue
series_b.source: Brad Feld, The Rule of 40% For a Healthy SaaS Company

metric.fr: Rule of 40

series_b.value: year-over-year ARR growth plus free cash flow margin should meet or exceed 40 %; the most reliable predictor of valuation over the past year
series_b.source: ICONIQ Growth, The ICONIQ Enterprise Five and State of Software 2025
series_b.note: 2025 edition; the page gives the year, not the day.

metric.fr: Magic number

series_b.value: change in subscription revenue between two quarters, annualised, over the sales and marketing spend of the earlier quarter; above 1x a compelling business, 0.5 to 1x probably successful but capital-inefficient, below 0.5x a model not yet figured out
series_b.source: Scale Venture Partners (Rory O'Driscoll), Magic Number Math

metric.fr: Magic number, médiane de long terme

series_b.value: long-term median around 0.7x, a fairly healthy efficiency baseline for most SaaS businesses; private-company magic numbers most recently trending down
series_b.source: Scale Venture Partners (Dale Chang), SaaS Metrics: A History of the Magic Number

metric.fr: Net magic number

series_b.value: current quarter net new ARR over prior quarter sales and marketing opex; top quartile companies have historically maintained a net magic number above 1.0x
series_b.source: ICONIQ Growth, The ICONIQ Enterprise Five
series_b.note: 2025 edition; the page gives the year, not the day. The net variant of C5.

metric.fr: Jeu de métriques du growth stage

series_b.source: a16z Growth, Introducing a16z Growth's Guide to Growth Metrics
series_b.note: Names the set (ARR growth, Rule of 40, gross margin, FCF margin, CAC payback, magic number, burn multiple, NDR) and says the 25th to 90th percentiles are in the guide, segmented by revenue scale and go-to-market motion; no figure on the page itself, and the trend matters more than the point. series_b.value: under 1.0x amazing, 1.0 to 1.5x great, 1.5 to 2.0x good, 2.0 to 3.0x suspect, above 3.0x bad; the multiple should fall as the company matures (a seed company might be at 3, after the series A it might drop to 2, after the series B efficiency expectations rise further) and a multiple going the wrong way as the startup matures indicates something is wrong
